newsitem.title: USA: Falcon Building to merge with Investcorp.
newsitem.headline: Falcon Building to merge with Investcorp.

text.p: Falcon Building Products Inc said Thursday it executed a definitive agreement to merge with Investcorp, an international investment group, in a transaction valued at about $590 million, including about $225 million of debt which will be refinanced.

The agreement provides that the owner of each Falcon common stock can choose either to receive $17.75 per share in cash or to retain that share. However, no more than 900,000 shares of Falcon common, or about four percent of the 20 million outstanding, may be retained by present Falcon shareholders.
The merger, expected to close in May, is subject to approval by a majority of Falcon's shareholders at a special meeting.

The board of Falcon has recommended that Falcon shareholders approve the merger. Falcon's major shareholder, which owns about 70 percent of the outstanding common stock, also has agreed to vote its shares in favor of the transaction.
Merrill Lynch & Co and Smith Barney Inc acted as financial advisors to Falcon and rendered a fairness opinion.

In connection with the transaction, all executive officers of Falcon, including president William Hall, have agreed to be employed by Falcon after the merger. Hall will be chairman, president and chief executive officer after completion of the merger.

Christopher Stadler, a member of Investcorp's management committee, said, "This acquisition is consistent with our philosophy of buying companies with leading market shares and trade names. As is our practice, we will work in partnership with management to continue Falcon's current growth initiatives and to provide whatever additional resources are necessary to enable the Company to achieve its potential."
Chicago-based Falcon, with 1996 annual sales of $633 million, is a manufacturer and supplier of highly engineered building products serving residential, light commercial and consumer markets.

Falcon businesses include Hart & Cooley, a manufacturer of air distribution products, Mansfield Plumbing Products, a manufacturer of china, steel and acrylic plumbing products, and DeVilbiss Air Power, a manufacturer of air compressors, pressure washers, portable generators and accessories/tools.
